newsitem.title: USA: Hilton extends ITT tender offer.
newsitem.headline: Hilton extends ITT tender offer.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp. on Thursday extended its $6.5 billion hostile bid for rival ITT Corp., marking the third time Hilton has been forced to extend the offer in its now-simmering takeover attempt for ITT.
Meanwhile, ITT said it would slash its New York headquarters staff to 75 from 200 as part of a strategy to raise shareholder value and improve profitability.
Hilton also said it has filed an appeal of a U.S. District Court ruling that thwarted Hilton's attempt to bring its proposed offer to a vote of ITT shareholders.

That ruling, issued Monday by Judge Philip Pro in Las Vegas, allows ITT to delay its annual meeting until mid-November, giving it time to sell assets and fend off Hilton's $55-per-share, cash and stock bid.

Beverly Hills, Calif.-based Hilton has extended the bid twice since proposing the deal Jan. 27. Thursday's move put a final date of May 30 on the offer. Only 1.5 million of about 122.7 million outstanding ITT shares have been tendered, unchanged from the last extension March 28.

Early in February, ITT, based in New York, rejected Hilton's bid as inadequate and set about refocusing its business on core hotel and gaming assets and selling non-core assets. ITT owns the Sheraton hotels and Caesars casinos.

It has since sold its stake in French Telecommunications company Alcatel Alstholm for $830 million and signed an agreement to sell its partnership position in Madison Square Garden Inc., owner of the famous sports arena, the New York Knicks professional basketball team and New York Rangers hockey team, for $650 million.

Hilton sued ITT in federal court, seeking to force ITT to hold its annual meeting in mid-May, when the shareholder gathering traditionally has been held. Hilton has nominated a slate of directors to unseat ITT's current board, and if elected, Hilton's directors would approve the offer.
In court, ITT argued that its bylaws and Nevada law allowed it to delay calling a meeting until mid-November, and Pro agreed. ITT still has not set a date for the meeting.
Hilton has said it will pursue its bid for ITT all the way to a shareholder vote.
In addition to the cuts in its headquarters staff, ITT said it would reduce occupancy at its posh midtown Manhattan headquarters to five floors from 11.
ITT Chairman Rand Araskog said it was offering employees whose jobs were being eliminated enhanced severance packages and retirement benefits as well as help getting other work.
A company spokesman said the cuts would result in a charge to first-quarter earnings, but declined to specify an amount.
Hilton stock closed down 50 cents at $26.375, and ITT stock ended off 25 cents at $58, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
